<description>
Since 4f1e6de6 (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/31507), cmake for visual studio can only generate projects that use clang-cl.
But calling cmake without '--preset windows' or '-T ClangCL' still silently generates projects that cannot build anymore.

For example, a build with cl now fails in minisketchwrapper.c because we don't pass anymore a cl option to set __cplusplus value properly.

I propose we explicitly tell at cmake time that this can't work anymore. If not, a lot of windows devs who use cmake without presets will lose time on this.
</description>

<commits>
eca1492f59 build: explicitly disable cl.exe

Since 4f1e6de6, cmake for visual studio can only generate projects that
use clang-cl.
But calling cmake without '--preset windows' or '-T ClangCL' still
silently generates projects that cannot build anymore.

Explicitly print a fatal error at cmake time if cl.exe is selected and
point to the doc.
</commits>

<files>
CMakeLists.txt  +7/-0

(test/bench/ci lines: 0)
</files>

<patch>
diff --git a/CMakeLists.txt b/CMakeLists.txt
index 7317dd3e13..d734c4e2ca 100644
--- a/CMakeLists.txt
+++ b/CMakeLists.txt
@@ -81,6 +81,13 @@ if(CMAKE_VERSION VERSION_LESS 4.2 AND CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Darwin" AND NO
 endif()
 enable_language(CXX)
 
+if(MSVC AND NOT CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID STREQUAL "Clang")
+  message(FATAL_ERROR
+  "Unsupported C++ compiler: ${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER}.\n"
+  "See the recommended doc/build-windows-native.md#building "
+  "or remove this check and continue at your own risk without support.")
+endif()
+
 set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
 set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
 set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

</patch>
